msgs.title: A position with five hedges on it is a knot, and knots only get tighter.
msgs.pub:
A position with five hedges on it is a knot, and knots only get tighter.

At Gordium stood an old cart tied with a knot nobody could undo.

The legend said whoever untied it would rule Asia.

Alexander studied it for a while, then drew his sword and cut it.

Traders tie the same knot. A losing stock, a put to protect it, a call sold to pay for the put, a roll to fix the call.

Each piece makes sense alone. Together they hide one fact. The trade is wrong.

I have spent weeks untying positions like that.

Selling the whole thing takes one click.

msgs.title: Plenty of investors sit in cash because two choices look equally good.
msgs.pub:
Plenty of investors sit in cash because two choices look equally good.

There is an old parable about a donkey, pinned on the philosopher Buridan by his critics.

It stands exactly between two equal piles of hay. It cannot pick one. It starves.

Markets punish that donkey every year.

Buy now and risk a drop. Wait and risk a rally. The two fears cancel, so nothing happens.

Waiting can be the right trade.

Waiting with no price and no date is the donkey's choice.

Pick a pile. Eat half now and the other half later.

msgs.title: Once you own a position, every new number gets cut to fit it.
msgs.pub:
Once you own a position, every new number gets cut to fit it.

The Greeks told of Procrustes, a host on the road to Athens.

He had one iron bed. Tall guests lost their feet. Short guests got stretched.

The bed never changed.

Investors do this with data. A weak print becomes noise. A strong one becomes proof.

I have stretched a few earnings reports myself to keep a stock I loved.

Theseus finished Procrustes by laying him on his own bed.

Lay your thesis on the data for once, and see what gets cut.

msgs.title: If you keep raising your limit on a stock that keeps running, you know this pain.
msgs.pub:
If you keep raising your limit on a stock that keeps running, you know this pain.

The Greeks gave it a name. Tantalus.

He stands in water up to his chin, under a tree heavy with fruit.

Each time he bends to drink, the water drains away. Each time he reaches, the branch lifts.

Chasing works the same way. You move the bid up, price moves faster, you move it again.

Sometimes the chaser does get filled. Usually at the top tick, right before the bull trap.

My rule is one entry price, written before the open. If it runs, I let it run without me.

The fruit you chase is priced for you.

msgs.title: When everyone waits for the pullback, the pullback stays small.
msgs.pub:
When everyone waits for the pullback, the pullback stays small.

The papers say a dip is due, so funds lighten up a little.

Retail sits on cash with a limit order a few percent lower.

Price slips, the orders fill, the shorts cover, and a week later the market is higher.

The dip everyone expects gets bought before it can grow.

In a real bull market, the waiting cash is the floor.

The deep drop comes later, once nobody is waiting for it anymore.

Now the louder the tip, the smaller I size.

msgs.title: Every sharp drop in a hot market gets called healthy within the hour.
msgs.pub:
Every sharp drop in a hot market gets called healthy within the hour.

I have heard that word for twenty years.

It was healthy for the shorts who sold near the top.

For the late bulls who bought on margin last week, it was a margin call.

Then price recovers, everyone relaxes, and the bears get laughed at again.

Nobody remembers who paid for the medicine.

Next time a desk calls a drop healthy, check your own size first.
